"Dunkirk" was released digitally on 12 December 2017, and on 4K Ultra HD, Blu-ray, and DVD on 18 December in the United Kingdom and 19 December in the United States. Dunkirk is a 2017 war film written, directed, and produced by Christopher Nolan that depicts the Dunkirk evacuation of World War II. Principal photography commenced on 23 May 2016 in Dunkirk, France. Production then continued for four weeks in Urk, Netherlands. Until 1475, the High and Low Lordship of Urk and Emmeloord was in the hands of the Van Kuinre family. The important economic pillar of the village is the fishery. After the IJsselmeer was formed, the people of Urk continued to fish on the North Sea. Cod, haddock, whiting, saithe, plaice, sole, mackerel, herring, pouting, sprat, and sandeel are all very common in the North Sea and are fished commercially. The North Sea yields millions of cubic metres of sand and gravel from the ocean floor each year, and rolled pieces of amber may also be found on nearby coasts. Storm surges threaten, in particular, the coasts around the North Sea, especially those of the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, and Denmark.
